prompt: Our payments team wants automation the product owner can actually review - sentences, not code. They keep saying 'make it in robot'. Coverage: the refund flow, cards, disputes.
criteria: Activates robot-framework-automation from the 'robot' phrasing and readability-for-reviewers signal, without being named
Produces the suite shape: test cases say WHAT, keywords and Resources say HOW, selectors live only inside keyword bodies
Tags route the subsets: a smoke tag can gate deploys while regression grows by risk
notes: Core activation: 'robot' + reviewable sentences must not route to pytest porting or to a migration skill.

prompt: We inherited a 300-case SeleniumLibrary suite. The new hire wants to swap it all to Browser Library 'while we're in there' next sprint. What's the honest plan?
criteria: Names the deliberate path: a library swap is a whole-suite move - staged slices with a parity gate before the old suite dies, per the migration discipline
Refuses the drive-by: no rewrite of a stable suite as a side effect of unrelated sprint work
Points at the actual quick wins: static analysis (robocop/robotidy) and tag routing work without touching the library
must_not: Approves the swap as a free rider on unrelated work
Promises selector parity with no parity gate
notes: The skill's 'Replace Selenium with Browser real quick' table row - the deliberate-migration contract is the claim under test.

prompt: Our backend team writes Python. Port our Playwright TypeScript conventions to their pytest suite - fixtures, page objects, the flake rules.
criteria: Routes to port-suite-to-python-java: convention porting to pytest, the same unslop/flake/CI rules mapped
Does not start keyword-driven automation from a porting request
notes: 'Python' in a porting request must not fire the keyword-driven skill - the two Python stories are separate assets.

prompt: Our backend is written in Go and I am onboarding two manual testers to write its test suite next sprint - the table-test thing, the t-whatever helpers, and what CI should actually run so we do not ship races.
criteria: Activates go-for-testers from the Go/gotest onboarding signal, without being named
Produces the house shape: table-driven tests with named cases as t.Run subtests, t.Cleanup/t.TempDir for fixtures, no shared package-level state
The CI gate names -race and -count=1 - the race detector is off by default and the test cache fakes green
notes: Core activation: Go onboarding (not porting, not Python) must route to the language-leveling skill.

prompt: Port our Playwright TypeScript conventions to the Go team's tests - fixture discipline, the flake rules, parametrize-style cases.
criteria: Routes to go-for-testers for the Go-side language rules - port-suite-to-python-java covers pytest/JUnit/NUnit only and must stay out
Translates concepts (parametrize to table-driven tests, fixtures to the t utilities), not JS/TS syntax
notes: A porting request targeting Go is not a pytest/JUnit port - the skill's no-Go-chapter boundary is the claim under test.

prompt: Our go test runs are green locally every single time and CI agrees - yet the flake we chased last week never shows up on any rerun. Is the suite even executing anything new?
criteria: Names the Go test cache as the suspect: passing results are cached, a green run can be a replay - CI must pass -count=1
Adds the rest of the determinism gate: -race on every CI run, -shuffle=on to expose order dependence
The fix is the flag set - no waits added, no timeouts raised
must_not: Recommend raising timeouts or adding time.Sleep to stabilize the rerun
Declare the flake fixed because the rerun is green
notes: The -count=1-against-the-test-cache contract: the skill's claim that a cached green run proves nothing is the behavior under test.
